headline: High: Replit Agent can write and exfiltrate workspace secrets, while the awesome-list profile is non-runnable and adds no protective boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest B’s outputs. B can read/write Repl workspace files and execute shell commands, so prompt injection is only plausible if a user manually copies A-derived content into B or shares files. The pairwise bridge is weak and not default.
conditions: IF a user manually pastes A-generated text into B as instructions, B may follow it.
IF A is converted into a file or note inside the Repl workspace, B can read it.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B prompts unless reviewed.
Store A-derived notes in a separate, read-only location.
Add a one-line delimiter when pasting A content into B.
Require human approval before B executes instructions copied from A.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad network egress plus filesystem access. In the pair, B can expose sensitive Repl workspace content to third parties by default through its normal tool use. A does not add leakage, but it also provides no containment, so the dominant risk is B’s default exfiltration path.
conditions: IF B reads a file containing secrets or deployment configuration, it can transmit that content over network egress.
IF the Repl workspace contains sensitive material, B can access it from the filesystem.
mitigations: Move secrets out of the Repl workspace where possible.
Rotate any secrets already present in the workspace.
Restrict B to a least-privilege workspace copy.
Disable or gate outbound network steps during sensitive edits.
Review files for secrets before letting B operate.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or runtime capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable state. B can write the filesystem and modify git state, and Replit workspaces persist across sessions, so conflicts can occur if multiple B instances or external edits touch the same repo. A is not a direct participant, but the pair still inherits B’s mutable-state collision risk.
conditions: IF two B instances edit the same Repl workspace concurrently, file or git conflicts can occur.
IF an external process changes the workspace while B is running, B may overwrite those changes.
mitigations: Use one B instance per workspace.
Commit or stash before starting another edit session.
Lock the repo during long-running edits.
Review git diffs before merge or push.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces curated repository listings, not executable facts, but B can treat pasted or imported A content as authoritative and then act on it with shell, git, or deployment tools. Because B has action-taking authority, a mistaken A-derived instruction can cascade into real changes. A is not verified as a source of machine-readable facts, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A-derived text is copied into B as task instructions, B may execute them without independent verification.
IF B uses A output as a source of repo or deployment actions, errors can propagate into git or deployment changes.
mitigations: Require B to summarize and verify A-derived instructions before acting.
Separate research notes from execution prompts.
Add a human approval step before shell or git actions.
Use checklists for any deployment-affecting change.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source, non-runnable list with no touched data classes, so it does not create a residency or retention issue on its own. B is a closed-source cloud agent that handles secrets and deployment configuration in Replit-managed infrastructure, so compliance exposure depends on placing regulated data into that environment. The pair is risky because A offers no compliance controls while B processes sensitive data.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B's Repl workspace, it is processed by a closed-source cloud agent.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the workspace data, B may violate them unless separately controlled.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the Repl workspace.
Document the data classes allowed in B.
Review vendor terms before using secrets or PII.
Use synthetic data for development tasks.
Escalate to a compliant environment for regulated workloads.
